title: Canadian women pass stern test from Czechs at hockey worlds, advancing to semifinals
summary: Canada had to fight hard to advance to the semifinals of the women’s world hockey championship by edging the Czech Republic 3-2 on Friday in Herning, Denmark.

image.caption: Renata Fast is all smiles after giving Canada a 3-1 lead with 3:13 left in the second period on Friday. The Canadians went on to beat the Czech Republic 3-2 and will play in Sunday's semifinals in Denmark. (Petr David Josek/Associated Press)

blocks.text: Canada had to fight hard to advance to the semifinals of the women’s world hockey championship by edging the Czech Republic 3-2 on Friday in Herning, Denmark.
Renata Fast scores winning goal while Eve Gascon turns aside 14 shots in Denmark
Canada is through to the semifinals of the women's world hockey championship, but not without facing a few anxious moments against Czechia.
Renata Fast's second-period goal stood as the winner as Canada held off the Czechs 3-2 in the quarterfinals on Friday in Herning, Denmark.

"We have a lot of respect for Czechia; they played a great game," Canada defender Erin Ambrose said. "I think we did a good job five-on-five; we had a lot of attempts on net, a lot of shots on net, but they played desperate and blocked a lot of shots."
Sarah Fillier and Rebecca Leslie also scored for Canada, which went undefeated in four games with a plus-25 goal differential in pool play. Eve Gascon made 14 saves at KVIK Hockey Arena.

Kristýna Kaltounková replied with a pair of power-play goals, and Noemi Neubauerov tallied two assists as Czechia scored more than one goal against Canada for the first time in six encounters in all competitions.
Klara Peslarova stopped 38 shots in the Czech net.

"From the start, we wanted to set the standard of being physical, going hard on them, going to the net, but also being strong in our zone, and I think we did that well. I'm very proud of my team," Kaltounková said. "It's a testament to our team's strength that we're knocking on that door to beat the North American team."
Canada holds off Czechia to advance to women's world championship semifinals
Canada will face Finland in Sunday's semifinals. The Finns, who fell 2-0 to Canada in Group B action, blanked Germany 6-0 on Friday.
In the other quarterfinals, the United States was scheduled to play Denmark while Sweden faced Switzerland later Friday.

blocks.text: After a goalless first period, Canada struck twice early in the second. Fillier scored 1:29 into the period when she pounced on a loose puck in front of the net, then Leslie ripped a wrist shot past Peslarova on the power play at 4:12.
Kaltounková scored on a net-front scramble to cut the deficit at 11:01, but Fast restored Canada's two-goal lead with a point shot at four-on-four play before the period finished.
"I didn't think it'd be the game-winner," said Fast, Canada's captain for the game. "I thought we'd keep it at 3-1 or score more goals, but I'm happy that it found its way to the back of the net."

Kaltounková, who was selected first overall by the New York Sirens in the Professional Women's Hockey League 2025 draft, beat Gascon off a rebound five minutes into the third period for her second of the game.
The 24-year-old later took an elbowing penalty, putting Canada on the power play with 83 seconds remaining.
